sentences.text: Caenagnathasia is a small theropod dinosaur belonging to the family Caenagnathidae, found in Uzbekistan during the Late Cretaceous.
It holds the record as the smallest known oviraptorosaur and ranks among the tiniest non-avian dinosaurs ever discovered.
The animal possessed three fingers on each hand and the same number on its feet, with bones fused in the same way as birds.
The dentary lacked teeth, making it the oldest known oviraptorosaur with this characteristic.
The known jaw fragments are only a few centimeters long, with an estimated total skull length of 3 inches.
A 2010 estimate by Gregory S. Paul suggested the animal was 2 feet long and weighed 3 pounds.
The species Caenagnathasia martinsoni was named and described in 1994 by Philip J. Currie, Stephen Godfrey, and Lev Nessov.
The genus is based on the holotype specimen N 401/12457, which consists of a pair of fused lower jaw bones.
The holotype was found near Dzharakuduk in the Bissekty Formation around 90 million years ago, making Caenagnathasia the oldest known caenagnathoid.
New material including vertebrae, a dentary, and a femur was described in 2015 from the same site as the original holotype.
The specific name honors Gerbert Genrikhovich Martinson.
A 2010 estimate by Gregory S. Paul gave it a length of 0.61 meters and a weight of 1.4 kg.
Specimens consisting mainly of lower jaws were initially assigned to birds by Sternberg in 1940 and Cracraft in 1971.
Caenagnathasia is a basal member of the family Caenagnathidae, and it is speculated that it is near the time when this family and Oviraptoridae separated.
It lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, 92 million years ago in the Turonian, in what is now Asia.
The time range for the genus is from the Turonian to the Campanian, between 93.9 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is speculated that Caenagnathasia lived near the time when the family Caenagnathidae and Oviraptoridae separated.
